title: Proof-of-Agentness: Towards Verifying Agents on the Web
title_zh: 智能体证明：面向网络上的智能体验证

paragraphs.en: CAPTCHAs and bot detection have helped protect Web services from automated abuse for decades by distinguishing humans from bots. However, the emergence of LLM-powered agents introduces a new setting: Web services increasingly accommodate agents as legitimate users. Without a way to distinguish agents from other automated clients such as simple bots and scripts, these services risk large-scale automated junk submissions that waste service resources and consume users’ attention or tokens. In this paper, we investigate a novel question for today’s Web: “How can a Web service obtain evidence that a client is an agent?” We introduce the concept of “Proof-of-Agentness” ( PoA ), a mechanism for distinguishing agents from other automated clients, motivated by the parallel between human attention and an agent’s inference resources. We outline two approaches: active verification through challenge–response and passive analysis of service-visible signals. Eight language models achieve an overall accuracy of 96.5% on our challenges, with an average overhead of 1,647 tokens. For passive analysis, we conduct an IRB-approved user study comparing the Web interactions of twelve human participants and representative Bot and Agent implementations, achieving an average classification accuracy of 95.8% across four classifiers, motivating further study.

paragraphs.en: CAPTCHAs and other bot detection mechanisms have helped protect human-facing Web services from automated abuse at scale by requiring evidence of human participation before granting access ( von Ahn et al., 2003 ; Park et al., 2006 ) . Each operation performed by a human consumes time and attention, while scripts can cheaply repeat requests and submissions, overwhelming services. These mechanisms aim to make access depend on evidence of human participation that bots cannot cheaply reproduce.
paragraphs.zh: CAPTCHA 等机器人检测机制通过在授予访问权限前要求提供人类参与的证据，帮助面向人类的网络服务免受大规模自动化滥用（von Ahn et al., 2003; Park et al., 2006）。 人类执行的每个操作都消耗时间和注意力，而脚本可以低成本地重复请求和提交，从而使服务不堪重负。 这些机制旨在让访问依赖于机器人无法低成本复现的人类参与证据。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, Web services are increasingly being designed for agents as well as humans. Cloudflare and Vercel serve agent-friendly Markdown pages ( Martinho and Allen, 2026 ; Cowan and Shah, 2026 ) . Many online services provide agent access through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), covering search (Brave, Exa, and Tavily) ( Brave, n.d. ; Exa, n.d. ; Tavily, n.d. ) ; data and knowledge queries (Hugging Face, Kaggle, Wikidata) ( Hugging Face, n.d. ; Kaggle, n.d. ; Wikidata contributors, n.d. ) ; payments (Stripe and PayPal) ( Stripe, 2026 ; PayPal, 2026 ) ; shopping (Shopify) ( Shopify, n.d. ) ; and development and workplace collaboration (GitHub, Notion, and Atlassian) ( GitHub, n.d. ; Notion, n.d. ; Atlassian, n.d. ) . However, these interfaces can also be used by ordinary programs. When agents rely on large language models (LLMs) to interpret tasks and choose actions, they consume inference compute and tokens ( Sardana et al., 2024 ) . A traditional automated program can avoid such resource costs and repeatedly submit requests directly, occupying server-side queues and consuming storage and computing resources. Junk submissions produced in this way can also require users or agents to spend attention or tokens processing their contents.

paragraphs.en: The resource analogy between human attention and model inference motivates our central research question: Can a Web service obtain evidence that a client is an agent and protect service capacity for useful agent work, just as CAPTCHAs and bot detection protect human-facing services for genuine human interaction?
paragraphs.zh: 人类注意力与模型推理之间的资源类比引出了我们的核心研究问题：网络服务能否获取证据证明客户端是智能体，并为有用的智能体工作保护服务容量，正如 CAPTCHA 和机器人检测保护面向人类的服务以供真实人类交互使用一样？

paragraphs.en: Agent verification is already entering Web infrastructure. Cloudflare’s Signed agents and Verified bots programs recognize agent traffic, and Web Bot Auth checks signed HTTP requests against registered public keys ( Lee, 2025 ; Cloudflare, 2026d ; Cloudflare, 2026e ) . However, these approaches authenticate identities asserted by agent operators or infrastructure providers without establishing actual agent participation. Recent studies also explore browser and behavioral fingerprints to distinguish Web agents from human users and other automated clients ( Wang et al., 2026 ; Fayolle et al., 2026 ) . These efforts advance agent recognition, but the positioning of agent verification on the Web remains unclear, and the concept itself is not yet fully developed.

paragraphs.en: Our Study In this paper, we introduce Proof-of-Agentness ( PoA ), which asks for evidence of language model participation in an interaction. We outline two design approaches: active verification that issues challenges to clients and checks their responses, and passive analysis using Web traffic and interaction characteristics. We then introduce a unified AgentScore that combines evidence for admission decisions. Such mechanisms could empower Web services to restrict access to agents acting on users’ behalf and regulate automated traffic more selectively, limiting large-scale scripted abuse of service resources.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的研究 在本文中，我们提出了智能体证明（Proof-of-Agentness，PoA），它要求提供语言模型参与交互的证据。 我们概述了两种设计方法：主动验证，即向客户端发出挑战并检查其响应；以及被动分析，即利用Web流量和交互特征进行分析。 随后，我们引入了一个统一的 AgentScore，它综合各类证据以做出准入决策。 此类机制可以帮助Web服务限制代表用户行事的智能体的访问，并更有选择地管控自动化流量，从而遏制对服务资源的大规模脚本化滥用。

paragraphs.en: Bot detection is a mechanism used by Web services to protect against large-scale automated abuse and attacks. Such systems examine request headers, browser characteristics, and behavior within sessions for signs of automation ( Park et al., 2006 ; Cloudflare, 2026a ) . Cloudflare, for example, combines known fingerprints, JavaScript checks, and machine-learning models to assign a bot score indicating how likely a request is to be automated ( Cloudflare, 2026b ) . A service may also use an explicit challenge to block automated traffic. CAPTCHAs follow this approach with tasks designed to be easy for humans and difficult for contemporary programs ( von Ahn et al., 2003 ) . The service checks the submitted response for admission control, admitting clients judged to be human.

paragraphs.en: Admission control can also make access conditional on computational effort. paragraphs.en: LLM-powered Web agents are becoming increasingly common on the Internet ( Conroy, 2026 ) . Moreover, multimodal agents such as WebVoyager and SeeAct incorporate visual observations to interpret webpages and select actions ( He et al., 2024 ; Zheng et al., 2024 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 由大语言模型驱动的网络智能体在互联网上正变得越来越常见（Conroy, 2026）。 在由大语言模型驱动的网络智能体中，语言模型解释用户指令并根据来自环境的观察选择动作（Gur et al., 2024；He et al., 2024）。 思维链（CoT）提示引导模型逐步推理（Wei et al., 2022），而 ReAct 则将推理、动作和观察结合起来（Yao et al., 2023）。 WebAgent 通过结合规划、HTML 理解和程序生成，将推理引入浏览器交互（Gur et al., 2024）。 此外，WebVoyager 和 SeeAct 等多模态智能体引入视觉观察来解读网页并选择动作（He et al., 2024；Zheng et al., 2024）。

paragraphs.en: A Web agent can access Web services through tools such as web_search and web_fetch ( Anthropic, n.d.d ; Anthropic, n.d.c ) , MCP interfaces ( Model Context Protocol, 2026 ) , browser extensions ( Anthropic, n.d.b ) , or browser-control and computer-use frameworks ( Browser Use, n.d.a ; Anthropic, n.d.a ) . To evaluate agents’ performance on Web tasks, researchers have developed a variety of Web-agent benchmarks. These include Mind2Web, WebArena, and WorkArena for Web tasks ( Deng et al., 2023 ; Zhou et al., 2024 ; Drouin et al., 2024 ) , VisualWebArena for visually grounded Web tasks ( Koh et al., 2024 ) , and OSWorld for broader computer-use tasks involving Web applications ( Xie et al., 2024 ) , showcasing the capabilities of LLM-powered agents across various domains and tasks.

paragraphs.en: Web platforms are introducing mechanisms to identify agents and authenticate their claimed identities. Cloudflare, for example, recognizes registered bots and agents through its Verified bots program, while Signed agents supports cryptographically authenticated agent traffic ( Cloudflare, 2026d ; Lee, 2025 ) . Web Bot Auth checks HTTP request signatures against registered public keys, allowing services to authenticate the sender associated with a claimed agent identity ( Cloudflare, 2026e ) .
paragraphs.zh: 各网络平台正在引入用于识别智能体并验证其声称身份的机制。 例如，Cloudflare 通过其「已验证机器人」计划识别已注册的机器人和智能体，而「签名智能体」则支持经过密码学认证的智能体流量（Cloudflare, 2026d; Lee, 2025）。 Web Bot Auth 通过对照已注册的公钥校验 HTTP 请求签名，使服务能够验证与所声称智能体身份相关联的发送者（Cloudflare, 2026e）。

paragraphs.en: Academic research also explores identity and authentication mechanisms for AI agents. For example, Garzon et al. propose a framework for agents to authenticate one another across organizational boundaries ( Garzon et al., 2026 ) . AgentDID uses decentralized identifiers and verifiable credentials to authenticate agent identities ( Xu et al., 2026 ) . Beyond identity authentication, several studies explore the use of fingerprints to identify AI browsing agents ( Wang et al., 2026 ; Fayolle et al., 2026 ; Lugoloobi et al., 2026 ) , reflecting research interest in this emerging area. However, identifying an agent or authenticating its identity does not by itself establish whether a language model participates in the current interaction. On the human-facing Web, account authentication verifies control of an account, but valid credentials can also be used by automated programs. CAPTCHAs and other bot detection mechanisms therefore seek evidence of human participation to limit automated abuse ( von Ahn et al., 2003 ; Cloudflare, 2026b ) . Similarly, an authenticated agent identity can also be used by a scripted program. This motivates a complementary mechanism for verifying model participation in agent-facing Web services.
paragraphs.zh: 学术研究还探索了面向智能体的身份与认证机制。 例如，Garzon 等人提出了一个框架，使智能体能够在组织边界之间相互认证（Garzon et al., 2026）。 AgentDID 使用去中心化标识符和可验证凭证来认证智能体身份（Xu et al., 2026）。 除身份认证之外，若干研究还探索利用指纹识别 AI 浏览智能体（Wang et al., 2026; Fayolle et al., 2026; Lugoloobi et al., 2026），反映出这一新兴领域的研究兴趣。 然而，识别智能体或认证其身份本身并不能确定某个语言模型是否参与了当前交互。 在面向人类的 Web 上，账户认证验证的是对账户的控制权，但有效的凭证也可能被自动化程序使用。 因此，CAPTCHA 等机器人检测机制试图寻找人类参与的证据，以限制自动化滥用（von Ahn et al., 2003; Cloudflare, 2026b）。 类似地，经过认证的智能体身份也可能被脚本化程序使用。 这就促使人们需要一种补充机制，用于在面向智能体的 Web 服务中验证模型参与。

paragraphs.en: Drawing inspiration from CAPTCHAs and bot detection, we propose Proof-of-Agentness ( PoA ) based on the resource analogy between human attention and language model inference. Human participation consumes time and attention, while language model participation consumes inference compute and tokens. Simple scripts can repeatedly submit requests at low marginal cost while occupying server-side queues and consuming storage and computing resources. PoA is designed to extend the principle of admitting humans while keeping bots out to agent-facing Web services. The goal is to admit agents while keeping automated bots out, empowering Web services to regulate automated traffic more selectively.
paragraphs.zh: 受 CAPTCHA 和机器人检测技术的启发，我们基于人类注意力与语言模型推理之间的资源类比，提出了智能体证明（Proof-of-Agentness，PoA）。 人类参与消耗时间和注意力，而语言模型参与消耗推理算力和 token。 简单脚本可以以较低的边际成本反复提交请求，同时占用服务器端队列并消耗存储和计算资源。 PoA 旨在将「放行人类、阻挡机器人」的原则扩展到面向智能体的 Web 服务。 其目标是放行智能体、阻挡自动化机器人，使 Web 服务能够更有选择性地管控自动化流量。

paragraphs.en: Requiring evidence of model participation could help agent-facing services prevent automated bots from gaining access by posing as agents, limiting opportunities for large-scale automated abuse at no cost. Such a mechanism can be deployed across Web interfaces, APIs, and MCP tools, particularly for operations that change service state, allocate limited resources, or directly affect other users. Services can specify which interactions or operations require evidence of model participation, making participation an explicit part of their access policies.
paragraphs.zh: 要求提供模型参与证明可以帮助面向智能体的服务防止自动化机器人伪装成智能体获取访问权限，从而在不增加成本的情况下限制大规模自动化滥用的机会。 这种机制可以部署在网页界面、API 和 MCP 工具中，尤其适用于那些会改变服务状态、分配有限资源或直接影响其他用户的操作。 服务可以指定哪些交互或操作需要提供模型参与证明，使模型参与成为其访问策略中一个明确的组成部分。

paragraphs.en: Hybrid policy. In practice, a service could use a hybrid policy to combine multiple sources of evidence, such as active challenge results, passive interaction signals, and verified agent declarations ( Cloudflare, 2026e ) . The policy could also incorporate existing access controls to govern access to protected operations. To support such hybrid policies, we introduce AgentScore , a unified score expressing the service’s confidence in recognizing a client as an Agent under its policy. If the score is too low to support the requested access, the service may defer its decision and request additional verification through an active challenge or an interaction probe . The resulting evidence updates AgentScore , allowing the service to reassess the request. Moreover, the permission granted should be bound to the authorized client and permitted operations, with expiry and usage limits. We detail the proposed scoring and access policy in Section 4.3 .
paragraphs.zh: 混合策略。 在实践中，服务可以采用混合策略来结合多种证据来源，例如主动质询结果、被动交互信号以及经验证的智能体声明（Cloudflare, 2026e）。 该策略还可以结合现有的访问控制来管理对受保护操作的访问。 为支持此类混合策略，我们提出 AgentScore，这是一个统一的分数，表示服务在其策略下识别客户端为智能体的置信度。 如果该分数过低而无法支持所请求的访问，服务可以推迟决策，并通过主动质询或交互探测请求额外的验证。 由此产生的证据会更新 AgentScore，使服务能够重新评估该请求。 此外，所授予的权限应绑定到经过授权的客户端和被允许的操作，并设置有效期和使用限制。 我们将在第 4.3 节详细说明所提出的评分与访问策略。

paragraphs.en: We implement active verification through challenge–response based on natural language understanding (NLU), a basic capability of language models. NLU tasks assess the interpretation of text and its implications ( Wang et al., 2019 ; Nie et al., 2020 ) , and carefully designed questions can expose the limitations of shallow rules and pattern matching ( McCoy et al., 2019 ; Levesque et al., 2012 ) . Structured simulations and templates also support the systematic generation of natural-language questions and test cases ( Weston et al., 2016 ; Ribeiro et al., 2020 ) .

paragraphs.en: This methodology begins with crafting narrative templates and their accompanying questions. Each template is a long passage with slots for entity names, attribute names, and values, and the questions contain corresponding slots. Each question has a natural-language form for presentation and a corresponding executable function f f for computing its answer once the slots are instantiated. For each challenge, a verifier uses a random seed to sample entities and attribute values from predefined sets, forming a world state W W that records the sampled entities and values. It uses this state to fill a selected narrative template and its question, producing a natural-language report R R and question q q . The verifier applies the function f f associated with q q to W W to compute the answer directly. The responding prover receives only the natural-language report and question. It is expected to reconstruct the relevant facts from the report and infer the question’s intended operation to derive its answer. Figure 3 illustrates this construction. paragraphs.en: Security assumptions. The construction relies on the assumption that language models can solve the generated challenges reliably, while simple rule-based programs cannot achieve comparable success. If this assumption holds, a correct response provides evidence of agent participation. Security also depends on keeping each random seed s s and the resource library ℒ \mathcal{L} private. Knowledge of both could allow an adversary to reproduce the world state and compute the answer directly. Repeated observations of public challenges may also reveal the library’s templates and question functions. The verifier should therefore periodically update or replace ℒ \mathcal{L} to make reconstruction from accumulated observations more difficult.

paragraphs.en: However, as LLM-powered agents become participants in Web traffic, it is still unclear whether they exhibit observable patterns distinct from those of humans and traditional bots. We started by reviewing Web access approaches available to agents in terms of their supported operations and service-visible signals, as summarized in Table 1 . Agents can use nearly all the access approaches listed, sharing interfaces with both humans and traditional bots. Their observable patterns can vary across interfaces and execution tools, overlapping with those of other client types. Automated scripts may also use agent-oriented interfaces and frameworks, such as MCP and Browser Use ( Model Context Protocol, 2026 ; Browser Use, n.d.b ) , to pose as agents. Agent verification on the Web fundamentally involves making a finer distinction between agents and bots within automated traffic. Reliable passive analysis generally relies on large, diverse, and representative datasets, which may give providers with broad visibility into Web traffic an advantage in developing and maintaining such models. paragraphs.en: Experimental setup. To collect behavioral data, we used the WebArena shopping website ( Zhou et al., 2024 ) , with three custom tasks: Wi-Fi adapters, USB drive, and wireless mice. paragraphs.en: We compare logistic regression ( LR ), random forest ( RF ), RBF-SVM ( Cortes and Vapnik, 1995 ) , and XGBoost ( Chen and Guestrin, 2016 ) using nested cross-validation. Each outer fold trains on two tasks and tests on the remaining task. paragraphs.en: Abuse Cost. An attacker may use a malicious agent or language model to solve a challenge while pursuing abusive goals. This is analogous to malicious humans passing CAPTCHAs themselves or outsourcing them to CAPTCHA-solving services ( Motoyama et al., 2010 ) . Such model use meets the participation requirement and incurs inference costs. Under the challenge assumptions, active verification could therefore raise the cost of access for clients that would otherwise rely entirely on scripts. Its practical value depends on whether this added cost changes the economics of large-scale abuse without imposing excessive overhead on agents performing normal tasks.
paragraphs.zh: 滥用成本。 攻击者可能出于滥用目的，使用恶意智能体或语言模型来解决挑战。 这类似于恶意人类自己通过验证码（CAPTCHA），或将验证码外包给验证码破解服务（Motoyama et al., 2010）。 此类模型使用满足了参与要求，并产生推理成本。 在挑战假设下，主动验证因此可以提高那些原本完全依赖脚本的客户端的访问成本。 其实际价值取决于这一新增成本能否改变大规模滥用的经济性，同时又不会给执行正常任务的智能体带来过高的开销。

paragraphs.en: Practical Deployment. Passive analysis uses evidence from ordinary interactions and can reduce verification overhead during normal agent activity. However, a script that is able to reproduce agent-like signals could also receive a high score without using a model. Stricter and more frequent verification could help maintain agent participation during continued access, but would also increase the burden on ordinary agents. The acceptability of this overhead could be explored in future deployments. paragraphs.en: Offline library construction. We prepare the library ℒ \mathcal{L} offline using LLM-generated materials from 5 domains: biochemistry, clinical trials, cybersecurity, financial markets, and food safety. Domain-specific prompts guide the LLM to generate entity names grouped by type and narrative templates with placeholders for entities, attributes, and values. For each template, the LLM also supplies possible attribute values and questions paired with functions that compute their answers from the world state . We implement rule-based checks to ensure consistent entity types and placeholders and verify that each question refers to facts included in its report. The resulting library contains 208 entities, 40 narrative templates, and 291 questions. At runtime, the verifier constructs each challenge at minimal cost by sampling from this library and instantiating the selected template.
paragraphs.zh: 离线构建题库。 我们使用大语言模型生成的来自 5 个领域的素材离线构建题库 ℒ \mathcal{L}：生物化学、临床试验、网络安全、金融市场和食品安全。 领域特定的提示词引导大语言模型生成按类型分组的实体名称，以及带有实体、属性和值占位符的叙事模板。 对于每个模板，大语言模型还会提供可能的属性值，以及与从世界状态 计算答案的函数配对的提问。 我们实施基于规则的检查，以确保实体类型和占位符的一致性，并验证每个提问都涉及包含在其报告中的事实。 最终的题库包含 208 个实体、40 个叙事模板和 291 个提问。 在运行时，验证器通过从该题库中采样并实例化所选模板，以最小成本构建每个挑战。

paragraphs.en: Challenge evaluation. We evaluate the models on 100 questions generated from 35 of the library’s 40 templates, with 20 questions from each domain. Of these questions, 60 ask for an attribute value, 20 compare two entities, and 20 ask for the entity with the highest or lowest value. All model queries go through OpenRouter ( OpenRouter, n.d. ) with the same structured-answer requirement and no model-specific sampling or reasoning settings. The verifier extracts the first submitted answer and normalizes Unicode, case, and whitespace without converting numbers or units. We report accuracy and latency over all 100 assigned questions, counting incorrect, empty, and filtered responses as failures. Each question contributes one selected response to the latency and token statistics. During evaluation, Claude did not answer 2 food-safety questions because of safety filtering. We count both as incorrect and retain their latency, while calculating Claude’s mean token usage from the 98 responses with reported usage.

paragraphs.en: Server overhead. We measure challenge assembly and answer checking on the same 100 questions using Python 3.9.6 on an Apple M5 running macOS arm64. The saved correct answers serve as inputs to the verifier. Each of the 3 independent Python processes loads resources and completes a warmup before timing. Batching calls reduces the overhead of clock and hardware-counter readings. For each question, we use the median per-call cost from the 3 runs; Table 3 summarizes these 100 estimates. To obtain combined overhead, we add each question’s assembly and verification costs within the same run before taking medians. The measurements exclude offline library preparation, resource loading, serialization, and HTTP serving. Instruction counts include the Python interpreter and operating-system work. Challenge and private-state sizes are measured using compact UTF-8 JSON serialization.

paragraphs.en: Each visit uses an independent guest shopping session. Automatic clients use new browser profiles or Cookie jars, while Human participants use their own browsers and may retain resource caches. For HTTP summaries, we retain application-page and API requests, including repetitions and failures, and exclude static resources, telemetry, and grading. The grader checks the final cart after observation closes. The analyzed dataset retains visits when clients do not complete the shopping tasks or their carts do not satisfy the task requirements. For 5 of the 72 Human visits, event recording was unexpectedly incomplete; we use the available observations and treat unavailable fields as missing. We exclude the HTTP-only Requests Bot from page-based classification.
paragraphs.zh: 每次访问使用一个独立的访客购物会话。 自动智能体使用新的浏览器配置文件或 Cookie 罐，而人类参与者使用自己的浏览器，并可能保留资源缓存。 对于 HTTP 摘要，我们保留应用页面和 API 请求（包括重复请求和失败请求），并排除静态资源、遥测数据和评分相关请求。 评分器在观察结束后检查最终购物车。 所分析的数据集会保留那些智能体未完成购物任务或其购物车不满足任务要求的访问。 在 72 次人类访问中，有 5 次的事件记录意外地不完整；我们使用可获得的观察数据，并将不可用的字段视为缺失。 我们将仅发出 HTTP 请求的 Requests Bot 排除在基于页面的分类之外。

paragraphs.en: To construct features, we apply log ⁡ ( 1 + x ) \log(1+x) to HTTP measurements, event counts, spans, and gap quantiles, keeping other features on their original scale. Timing and sequence measurements use click, input, and scroll events, with adjacency reset at document boundaries. The collector records pointer-move and scroll events at most once every 100 ms each. Within each training split, we estimate preprocessing parameters and class weights, filling missing fields with the observed means without adding missingness indicators. LR and RBF-SVM also use standardization fitted on that split. The predictors exclude identifiers and proxy-side connection counts, along with model-side logs and task grades.
paragraphs.zh: 在构造特征时，我们对 HTTP 测量值、事件计数、span 以及间隔分位数应用 log ⁡ ( 1 + x ) \log(1+x) 变换，其余特征保持其原始尺度。 时序与序列测量使用 click、input 和 scroll 事件，并在文档边界处重置邻接关系。 采集器对 pointer-move 和 scroll 事件各自最多每 100 ms 记录一次。 在每个训练划分内，我们估计预处理参数和类别权重，用观测均值填充缺失字段，且不添加缺失指示变量。 LR 和 RBF-SVM 还使用在该划分上拟合的标准化。 预测变量排除了标识符和代理侧连接计数，以及模型侧日志和任务评分。

paragraphs.en: Within each outer training set, we alternate the 2 tasks between inner training and validation, using P01–P04 for Human training visits and P05–P08 for validation visits. We select among 6 prespecified candidates per classifier and feature setting by mean inner-validation macro-F1, breaking ties by candidate order, and then refit the selected classifier on all outer training data. To supplement the interaction records, we measure TLS/HTTP fingerprints before proxy rewriting using 33 separate HTTPS probes: 3 per automatic configuration and 3 each for ordinary Chrome and Safari. In Table 5 , these reference browsers supply the Human fingerprints, while the 72 participant visits provide the Human HTTP statistics.
paragraphs.zh: 在每个外层训练集内，我们在内层训练与验证之间交替使用这两个任务，其中 Human 训练访问使用 P01–P04，验证访问使用 P05–P08。 我们针对每种分类器与特征设置，依据内层验证平均 macro-F1 在 6 个预设候选中进行选择，出现平局时按候选顺序决定，然后在全部外层数据上重新拟合所选分类器。 为补充交互记录，我们在代理改写之前使用 33 次独立的 HTTPS 探测测量 TLS/HTTP 指纹：每种自动配置 3 次，普通 Chrome 和 Safari 各 3 次。 在表 5 中，这些参考浏览器提供 Human 指纹，而 72 次参与者访问提供 Human HTTP 统计数据。
